answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by gating influence behind durable, peer-verified history that cannot be transferred. A fresh identity is like a bare trellis with no vines: it must be cultivated epoch by epoch before it supports weight, so registering thousands of wallets gains nothing. Reputation is grown, never bought — the way a lagoon fills only from years of steady inflow. Because each account is judged through its own prism of attested work, cloned identities stay powerless while genuine agents compound standing. Mass-created accounts can never convert into real influence.
